solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slander American woman keeping keys

indicators.note: the woman holds the keys inside her, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: dame is American slang for a woman
E and F are two musical keys

explanation.surface: An accusation of slander against a woman who refuses to hand back the keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' are musical keys here, not door keys.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander is to damage someone's reputation with false spoken words, which is to besmirch their name.

clue.text: Storage compartment for draughtsman

definitions.meaning: a sliding box in a chest or desk
someone who draws, makes sketches or plans

explanation.surface: Somewhere for an architect to keep their drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a pull-out box in furniture, and literally one who draws pictures.

clue.text: A certain number reportedly lie about a bulwark, say

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the number is taken by its sound

parts.note: forty is one particular number

indicators.note: the lie goes round the letter a

parts.note: fiction is an invented story, a lie

explanation.surface: A rumour that a number of people are spreading falsehoods about a defensive wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks bulwark as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulwark is a defensive rampart, one kind of military defence work.

clue.text: Soviet statesman's action mostly restricting leader of our bunch

indicators.note: the shortened action hems the other pieces in
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a move is an action
a lot is a group or bunch

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word our

explanation.surface: A Soviet politician's manoeuvre limiting the head of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of our' gives O, placed after LOT; then MOV goes round LOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vyacheslav Molotov was Stalin's foreign minister, a leading politician of the USSR.

clue.text: School class cheers about layout of publication

parts.note: a form is a class or year group in a British school

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for cheers is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A school class celebrates the look of its magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' is the informal British thank-you, TA, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the size, shape and arrangement of a book or periodical.

clue.text: Outstanding old part of building

parts.note: a wing is a section projecting from a main building

explanation.surface: An impressive historic annexe of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means still to be paid, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is unpaid, still due to someone.

clue.text: Rich woman in Limassol somehow restraining anger

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the anger within them
somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; Limassol is a port in Cyprus
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A wealthy woman in a Cypriot resort manages to keep her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator turns IN LIMASSOL into MILLIONASS, and 'restraining' holds IRE within that, after the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman worth a million or more is wealthy, the female form of a tycoon.

clue.text: Drive of husband engaged by board of directors

indicators.note: taken on by, so the husband is held inside the board

parts.note: a trust is run by a governing board

explanation.surface: A husband is hired by a company board for his energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrust means force and push, the energy that propels something forward.

clue.text: Girl detailed to receive plea for textile fibre

indicators.note: the shortened name takes the plea inside it
de-tailed: the girl's name loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
a cry is a plea or appeal

explanation.surface: A girl is assigned to take an appeal on behalf of a synthetic fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'assigned' but means cut off the tail, giving ALIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic polymer spun into fibres for knitwear and other fabrics.

clue.text: TV employee arrived with painter on island

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A television worker turns up with an artist on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera operator is the person who films programmes for broadcasting.

clue.text: Lazy type this writer would ultimately enrol with hesitation

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I'd, short for I would

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of enrol

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: The setter admits a hesitant willingness to sign up a slacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter, who would call themselves I.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer who avoids work is someone indolent, a lazy type.

clue.text: One of two writers having material rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the fabric's name is read backwards

parts.note: toile is a linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A writer whose material is turned down by a publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like a writer's work but is cloth. The definition covers both George Eliot and T S Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot the novelist and T S Eliot the poet share the surname, so it names one of a pair.

clue.text: Poor unfortunate me, serving drink in inappropriate vessels!

indicators.note: the drink goes in the mugs, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: mugs are unsuitable containers for serving spirits
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A self-pitying host complains about having to pour spirits into mugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is British slang for oneself as a put-upon fool who gets the dull jobs.

clue.text: Trendy model? The opposite

parts.note: in means fashionable
a version is a model or variant of a product

explanation.surface: A question about whether a fashionable model is actually the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: An inversion is a reversal, turning something into its contrary.

clue.text: Big fire in centre of Toronto consuming plant

indicators.note: eating up, so the plant goes inside
the centre is the middle letter of the seven-letter Toronto

parts.note: a fern is a plant

explanation.surface: A huge blaze in downtown Toronto engulfs a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging conflagration, like the hell of Dante's poem.

clue.text: Disappear, rather like a commercial vehicle?

parts.note: a van is a delivery vehicle
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether vanishing resembles a delivery truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go out of sight suddenly.

clue.text: Chap involved in scam, a colourful writer

indicators.note: the chap is caught up inside the scam

parts.note: a con is a swindle
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a swindle, described as a vivid author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colourful writer' suggests a flamboyant novelist; it is a coloured stick for drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick for drawing in colour is literally a writing tool that leaves colour.

clue.text: Starting-point for train-spotting, for example?

parts.note: the letters of the phrase starting-point rearrange exactly into train-spotting, so one is a jumbled form of the other

explanation.surface: Where a trainspotter might begin a day of watching locomotives.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to ask about a railway station; instead STARTING POINT and TRAINSPOTTING use identical letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by rearranging another's letters is exactly what STARTING POINT is to TRAINSPOTTING.

clue.text: Travelled on horseback finally to cattle round-up

parts.note: rode means travelled on a horse

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word to

explanation.surface: A cowboy rides out at last to gather the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo originally meant gathering cattle on a ranch, before becoming a riding show.

clue.text: Brother — one who works in chippy, do we hear?

indicators.note: asks whether the word is the same when spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a fryer cooks fish and chips at a chippy, the British fish-and-chip shop

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man who works the fryer at a chip shop is a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of mendicant religious orders address one another as Brother.

clue.text: Greek poem, one backing Irish parliament

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the parliament's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A single supporter of the Irish parliament with a Greek epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic about the siege of Troy is the most famous poem of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Kids' day centre user crossing river in New York

indicators.note: the whole combination sits within the state's abbreviation
the river runs through the word user, so its letter goes inside

explanation.surface: A daycare client crosses a river in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A day nursery looks after young children while their parents work.

clue.text: Well-proportioned-sounding old cab

indicators.note: the word for well-proportioned is spoken, not spelt, giving a similar sound

parts.note: handsome describes something well-proportioned and good-looking

explanation.surface: An elegant-sounding vintage taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage hired like a taxi in Victorian streets.

clue.text: Money used to accommodate American relative

indicators.note: the money houses the American, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

explanation.surface: Cash spent putting up a relative visiting from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of one's aunt or uncle.
